name: 서린

tips.동사·시제: 과거 이야기는 끝까지 과거형! 현재와 섞지 않기. 일반동사 앞에 I'm 붙이지 않기. used to + 동사원형 / be used to + -ing.
tips.단어 선택: every + 단수명사: every day. stress(명사)·stressed(사람)·stressful(일), affect(동사)·effect(명사) 구분.
tips.관사·전치사: listen to music. 신분 앞에 a: a high school student. take the bus.
tips.문장 구조: prefer + -ing: I prefer taking the bus. 주어 먼저: The subway is more convenient.

focus.1: Part 1 Study·Hometown 질문은 3줄씩 말할 수 있게 연습하기!
focus.2: used to + 동사원형(예전에 ~했다) vs be used to + -ing(~에 익숙하다) 구분! 거리는 It takes 20 minutes on foot / It's a 20-minute walk 두 가지로.

compare: It's a 5-minute walk. minute 단수 · It takes 5 minutes on foot. minutes 복수
used to + 동사원형 예전에 ~했다 · be used to + -ing ~에 익숙하다
내 기분은 -ed: I'm bored · 그게 주는 느낌은 -ing: It's boring

cards.ko: 간호사로서 가장 중요한 건 마음챙김이에요
cards.en: The most important thing as a nurse is mindfulness.
cards.gram: The most important thing as a + 직업 + is ~ = ~로서 가장 중요한 건 ~예요. Work 질문에 그대로 쓰세요.

cards.ko: 환자를 돌보기 전에 우리 스스로를 돌볼 줄 알아야 해요
cards.en: We need to know how to take care of ourselves before we take care of our patients.
cards.gram: know how to + 동사 = ~할 줄 알다. take care of = 돌보다.

cards.ko: 저는 혼자 살고 싶어요
cards.en: I want to live on my own.
cards.gram: 혼자 = on my own. 같은 뜻으로 by myself도 써요. 예: I like travelling on my own.

cards.ko: 저는 밤형 인간이에요
cards.en: I'm a night owl.
cards.gram: night owl = 밤에 활동하는 사람. 반대는 morning person.

cards.ko: 소음 때문에 잠을 잘 못 자요
cards.en: I can't sleep well because of the noise.
cards.gram: noise = 소음(셀 수 없음). because of + 명사.

cards.ko: 어렸을 때 저는 밖에서 노는 걸 정말 좋아했어요
cards.en: When I was young, I really loved playing outside.
cards.gram: 과거 이야기는 처음부터 끝까지 과거형! when I was young (was 빠뜨리지 않기).

cards.ko: 저는 보통 아침에 커피를 마셔요
cards.en: I usually drink coffee in the morning.
cards.gram: 일반동사(drink) 앞에 I'm을 붙이지 않아요. 습관은 현재형.

cards.ko: 저는 매일 산책해요
cards.en: I go for a walk every day.
cards.gram: every + 단수명사: every day, every week. everydays ❌. '매일'은 띄어서 every day.

cards.ko: 제 고향에는 공항이 있어요
cards.en: My hometown has an airport.
cards.gram: 주어가 하나(my hometown)면 has. 모음 앞 관사는 an airport.

cards.ko: 병원까지 걸어서 5분이에요 (It's a ~ walk로)
cards.en: It's a 5-minute walk to the hospital.
cards.gram: a 5-minute walk: 숫자-minute는 하이픈으로 연결하고 minute는 단수. walk 자리에 drive, bus ride도 넣을 수 있어요.
cards.mine: It take a 5 minute to the hospital for a walk.

cards.ko: 병원까지 걸어서 5분 걸려요 (It takes로)
cards.en: It takes 5 minutes on foot to get to the hospital.
cards.gram: It takes + 시간 + on foot = 걸어서 ~ 걸린다. 여기선 minutes 복수. takes의 s 빠뜨리지 않기.

cards.ko: 회사까지 지하철로 15분이에요
cards.en: It's a 15-minute subway ride to work.
cards.gram: 교통수단이면 walk 대신 subway ride / bus ride / drive. It takes로 바꾸면: It takes 15 minutes by subway.

cards.ko: 저는 불면증이 있어요
cards.en: I have insomnia.
cards.gram: 병 이름(insomnia)에는 보통 a를 안 붙여요. 철자: in-som-ni-a.

cards.ko: 그래서 다른 방법을 써 봤어요
cards.en: So I tried a different way.
cards.gram: 다른 방법 = another method / a different way. tried to 뒤엔 동사원형이 와야 해요.

cards.ko: 저는 스트레스를 줄이려고 마음챙김 명상을 해요.
cards.en: I practise mindfulness to reduce stress.
cards.gram: mindfulness = 마음챙김. 내 단어장 단어로 만든 새 문장이에요.

cards.ko: 우리 동네는 밤에 소음이 거의 없어요.
cards.en: There's hardly any noise in my neighbourhood at night.
cards.gram: noise = 소음. 내 단어장 단어로 만든 새 문장이에요.

cards.ko: 저는 밤형 인간이라 밤에 공부가 더 잘 돼요.
cards.en: I'm a night owl, so I study better at night.
cards.gram: night owl = 밤형 인간. 내 단어장 단어로 만든 새 문장이에요.

cards.ko: 야간 근무 후에는 가끔 불면증이 생겨요.
cards.en: I sometimes get insomnia after night shifts.
cards.gram: insomnia = 불면증. 내 단어장 단어로 만든 새 문장이에요.

cards.ko: 주말에는 혼자 산책하는 걸 좋아해요.
cards.en: I like going for walks on my own at the weekend.
cards.gram: on my own = 혼자서. 내 단어장 단어로 만든 새 문장이에요.

cards.ko: 저는 간호사가 되고 싶었어요.
cards.en: I wanted to become a nurse.
cards.gram: want to become + 직업 = ~가 되고 싶다. 과거 이야기라 wanted.

cards.ko: 환자들이 회복하는 걸 볼 때 뿌듯해요.
cards.en: I feel proud when I see my patients recover.
cards.gram: feel proud when ~ = ~할 때 뿌듯하다. see + 사람 + 동사원형: see my patients recover.

cards.ko: 우리가 우리 자신을 돌볼 줄 모르면, 그들도 돌볼 수 없을 거예요.
cards.en: If we don't know how to take care of ourselves, we won't know how to take care of them.
cards.gram: If + 현재, won't + 동사 = ~하면 ~하지 못할 거예요. know how to + 동사 = ~할 줄 알다.

cards.ko: 우리 도시에는 기차 노선이 하나밖에 없어요.
cards.en: There is only one train line in my city.
cards.gram: There is only one + 단수명사 = ~이 하나밖에 없다. train line = 기차 노선.

cards.ko: 걸어서 20분 걸려요.
cards.en: It takes 20 minutes on foot.
cards.gram: It takes + 시간 + on foot. 여기서는 minutes 복수.

cards.ko: 걸어서 20분 거리예요.
cards.en: It's a 20-minute walk.
cards.gram: It's a 20-minute walk. 숫자-minute이 형용사라 minute 단수!

cards.ko: 저는 버스 타는 걸 더 좋아해요.
cards.en: I prefer taking the bus.
cards.gram: prefer + -ing(또는 to + 동사). 교통수단 앞에 the: take the bus.

cards.ko: 저는 지하철에서 음악을 들어요.
cards.en: I listen to music on the subway.
cards.gram: listen to + 대상. to를 빼먹지 않기! 교통수단 안에서는 on the subway.

cards.ko: 지하철이 더 편리해요.
cards.en: The subway is more convenient.
cards.gram: 주어(The subway) + 동사(is) + 형용사 순서로. convenient는 긴 형용사라 more convenient.

cards.ko: 고등학생 때 저는 공부를 많이 했어요.
cards.en: When I was a high school student, I studied a lot.
cards.gram: 사람·신분 앞에 a: a high school student. high school은 두 단어.

cards.ko: 예전에는 커피를 많이 마셨어요.
cards.en: I used to drink a lot of coffee.
cards.gram: used to + 동사원형 = 예전에는 ~했다(지금은 아님).

cards.ko: 저는 야간 근무에 익숙해요.
cards.en: I'm used to working night shifts.
cards.gram: be used to + -ing = ~하는 데 익숙하다. used to 동사원형(예전에 ~했다)과 구분!

cards.ko: 어릴 때 저는 밤에 일찍 잤어요.
cards.en: I used to go to bed early when I was a child.
cards.gram: used to + 동사원형 = 예전에는 ~했다(지금은 아님). 어릴 때 습관 말할 때 딱 좋아요.

cards.ko: 예전에는 학교까지 걸어서 다녔어요.
cards.en: I used to walk to school.
cards.gram: used to + 동사원형 = 예전에는 ~했다(지금은 아님).

cards.ko: 예전엔 피를 보면 무서웠는데, 지금은 괜찮아요.
cards.en: I used to be scared of blood, but now I'm fine.
cards.gram: used to + 동사원형 = 예전에는 ~했다(지금은 아님). be동사도 가능: used to be + 형용사.

cards.ko: 저는 하루 종일 서 있는 데 익숙해요.
cards.en: I'm used to standing all day.
cards.gram: be used to + -ing = ~하는 데 익숙하다. to 뒤에 -ing! 간호사 Work 답변에 쓰세요.

cards.ko: 저는 아직 이른 아침에 일어나는 게 익숙하지 않아요.
cards.en: I'm not used to getting up early yet.
cards.gram: be used to + -ing = ~하는 데 익숙하다. to 뒤에 -ing! 부정은 I'm not used to + -ing.

cards.ko: 저는 혼자 사는 데 익숙해요.
cards.en: I'm used to living on my own.
cards.gram: be used to + -ing = ~하는 데 익숙하다. to 뒤에 -ing! on my own = 혼자.

cards.ko: 야간 근무에 익숙해지는 데 몇 달 걸렸어요.
cards.en: It took me a few months to get used to working night shifts.
cards.gram: get used to + -ing = ~하는 데 익숙해지다(익숙해지는 과정). It took me + 기간 + to 동사 = ~하는 데 ~가 걸렸다.

cards.ko: 저는 영어로 말하는 데 점점 익숙해지고 있어요.
cards.en: I'm getting used to speaking English.
cards.gram: get used to + -ing = ~하는 데 익숙해지다(익숙해지는 과정). 진행형 I'm getting used to = 점점 익숙해지고 있다.

cards.ko: 예전에는 커피를 안 마셨는데, 지금은 커피 없이는 못 살아요.
cards.en: I didn't use to drink coffee, but now I can't live without it.
cards.gram: used to + 동사원형 = 예전에는 ~했다(지금은 아님). 부정은 didn't use to(d 없이 use).

cards.ko: 제 일은 스트레스가 많아서 가끔 스트레스를 받아요.
cards.en: My job is stressful, so I sometimes feel stressed.
cards.gram: stressful = (일·상황이) 스트레스를 주는, stressed = (사람이) 스트레스 받은, stress = 명사.

cards.ko: 스트레스는 제 잠에 영향을 줘요.
cards.en: Stress affects my sleep.
cards.gram: affect = 영향을 주다(동사), effect = 영향, 효과(명사).

cards.ko: 야간 근무는 제 건강에 큰 영향을 줘요.
cards.en: Night shifts have a big effect on my health.
cards.gram: have an effect on ~ = ~에 영향을 주다. effect는 명사!

cards.ko: 우리는 같은 기수였어요.
cards.en: We were in the same batch.
cards.gram: batch = 동기, 기수. She is my batchmate.

cards.ko: 지금 7시 10분 전이에요.
cards.en: It's ten to seven.

cards.ko: 가격 면에서는 꽤 싸요.
cards.en: Price-wise, it's quite cheap.
cards.gram: 명사 + -wise = ~ 면에서: price-wise, location-wise.

cards.ko: 저는 편식 안 해요.
cards.en: I'm not a picky eater.
cards.gram: picky eater = 편식하는 사람. Food 질문에 바로 쓰세요.

cards.ko: 우리 도시는 아이를 키우기 좋은 곳이에요.
cards.en: My city is a good place for bringing up children.
cards.gram: a good place for -ing = a good place to + 동사원형. bring up = (아이를) 키우다.

cards.ko: 우리 도시에는 병원이 많아요.
cards.en: There are many hospitals in my city.
cards.gram: ❌ many hospital → ✅ many hospitals. many 뒤에는 꼭 복수형!

cards.ko: 저는 큰 도시에 사는 걸 더 좋아해요.
cards.en: I prefer living in a big city.
cards.gram: ❌ prefer live → ✅ prefer living. prefer 뒤에는 -ing (또는 to live).

cards.ko: 저는 이 도시에서 5년째 살고 있어요.
cards.en: I have been living in this city for five years.
cards.gram: have been -ing = 지금까지 쭉 ~하고 있다. 꿀팁: have been = am으로 생각! I am living이 되니까 I have been living도 OK.

cards.ko: 저는 집에서 식물을 키워요.
cards.en: I grow plants at home.
cards.gram: 식물은 grow. ❌ grow up plants (grow up = 사람이 자라다).

cards.ko: 저는 강아지를 한 마리 키워요.
cards.en: I have a dog.
cards.gram: 동물을 키운다 = have a dog (raise a dog도 가능).

cards.ko: 지난주에 식물이 죽어서, 지금은 죽어 있어요.
cards.en: My plant died last week, so now it's dead.
cards.gram: die = 죽다(동사) / dead = 죽은(형용사). it's died ❌ → it's dead.

cards.ko: 저는 일주일에 두 번 식물에 물을 줘요.
cards.en: I water my plants twice a week.
cards.gram: water = 물을 주다(동사로도 써요).

cards.ko: 이 꽃은 향기가 정말 좋아요.
cards.en: This flower has a lovely scent.
cards.gram: scent / fragrance = 좋은 향기. smell보다 고급스러운 말.

cards.ko: 저는 주말에 쇼핑하러 가요.
cards.en: I go shopping at the weekend.
cards.gram: ❌ go to shopping → ✅ go shopping. go swimming, go hiking도 같은 패턴!

cards.ko: 저는 집에 있는 걸 정말 좋아해요.
cards.en: I really like staying at home.
cards.gram: ❌ like stay → ✅ like staying (또는 like to stay).

cards.ko: 온라인 쇼핑의 장점은 편리하다는 거예요.
cards.en: The benefit of shopping online is that it's convenient.
cards.gram: The benefit of -ing is that ~ = ~의 장점은 …라는 거예요. 복수로 말하면 The benefits … are.

cards.ko: 스트레스를 받을 때마다 저는 산책을 해요.
cards.en: Whenever I feel stressed, I go for a walk.
cards.gram: Whenever + 문장 = ~할 때마다.

cards.ko: 야간 근무가 끝날 때마다 저는 녹초가 돼요.
cards.en: Whenever I finish a night shift, I feel exhausted.
cards.gram: Whenever + 문장, 결과 문장. exhausted = 녹초가 된.

cards.ko: 제가 집에 갈 때마다 엄마가 맛있는 걸 해 주세요.
cards.en: Whenever I go home, my mom cooks something delicious for me.
cards.gram: Whenever 다음은 현재형(습관). cook something for 사람 = ~에게 뭔가 요리해 주다.

cards.ko: 야간 근무는 제 잠에 큰 영향을 줘요.
cards.en: Night shifts have a big impact on my sleep.
cards.gram: have an impact on ~ = ~에 영향을 주다 (= affect, affect on ❌).

cards.ko: 야간 근무 후에는 잠들기가 어려워요.
cards.en: I find it hard to fall asleep after a night shift.
cards.gram: find it hard to + 동사원형 = ~하는 게 어렵다.

cards.ko: 저는 가족과 좋은 시간을 보내려고 해요.
cards.en: I try to spend quality time with my family.
cards.gram: quality time = (짧아도) 알찬 시간. quality sleep = 양질의 잠.

cards.ko: 식물을 키우려면 적절한 물, 햇빛, 온도가 필요해요.
cards.en: To grow plants, you need the right amount of water, sunlight, and the right temperature.
cards.gram: To + 동사원형, = ~하려면(목적). the right amount of ~ = 적절한 양의 ~. sunlight(햇빛), temperature(온도).

cards.ko: 시간이 날 때마다 저는 식물에 물을 줘요.
cards.en: Whenever I have time, I water my plants.
cards.gram: Whenever + 문장 = ~할 때마다.

cards.ko: 피곤할 때마다 저는 커피를 마셔요.
cards.en: Whenever I feel tired, I drink coffee.
cards.gram: Whenever I feel + 형용사 = ~할 때마다.

cards.ko: 비가 올 때마다 저는 집에 있는 게 좋아요.
cards.en: Whenever it rains, I like staying at home.
cards.gram: 날씨는 it으로: Whenever it rains. like staying (like stay ❌).

cards.ko: 친구들을 만날 때마다 우리는 카페에 가요.
cards.en: Whenever I meet my friends, we go to a café.
cards.gram: Whenever 다음 현재형 = 습관.

cards.ko: 잠이 안 올 때마다 저는 책을 읽어요.
cards.en: Whenever I can't fall asleep, I read a book.
cards.gram: fall asleep = 잠들다. Whenever I can't ~ = ~하지 못할 때마다.

cards.ko: 환자들이 회복하는 걸 볼 때마다 뿌듯해요.
cards.en: Whenever I see my patients recover, I feel proud.
cards.gram: see + 사람 + 동사원형 = ~가 …하는 것을 보다. feel proud = 뿌듯하다.

cards.ko: 어렸을 때 저는 할머니 댁에 갈 때마다 꽃을 심었어요.
cards.en: When I was young, whenever I visited my grandma, I planted flowers.
cards.gram: 과거 습관은 과거형으로: whenever I visited, I planted (시제 맞추기!).

groups.title: Home · Hometown
qs: Where are you from?
Which city are you living in?
Do you know any history about your hometown?
Do you prefer to live in an apartment or in a house?
Who do you live with?
Are there many rooms in your home?
What is your favourite room?
What would you change about your home?
How are the walls decorated?
How could your hometown be improved?
Is there good public transport in your hometown?
What's your neighbourhood like?
Do you think your hometown is a good place to bring up children?

groups.title: Study
qs: Do you study or work?
What do you study?
Why did you choose that subject?
Is it a popular subject in your country?
Do you plan to get a job in the same field as your subject?

groups.title: Work
qs: Why did you choose that job?
Do you like your job?
Where do you work?
Do you plan to continue with your job in the future?
What responsibilities do you have at work?

groups.title: Sleep
qs: How many hours do you usually sleep?
Are you a morning person or a night owl?
Do you ever take naps during the day?
What do you do when you can't fall asleep?
Did you sleep more when you were a child?
Do you think people sleep less these days than in the past? Why?

groups.title: Neighbours
qs: Do you know your neighbours well?
How often do you see your neighbours?
Have your neighbours ever helped you?
What makes a good neighbour?
Did you get on with your neighbours when you were a child?
Do you think people care less about their neighbours nowadays?

groups.title: Gifts
qs: Do you like giving gifts to others?
What was the last gift you received?
Do you prefer giving or receiving gifts?
What gifts are popular in your country?
Have you ever received a gift you didn't like?
Do you think expensive gifts are always better? Why?

groups.title: Time management
qs: Are you usually on time?
Do you make plans for your day?
How do you feel when you are late?
What do you usually do in your free time?
Do you think it's important to be punctual? Why?
If you had more free time, what would you do?

groups.title: Transport
qs: How do you usually get to work?
